problem_text: Let A be a Noetherian local ring such that its completion Â is a unique factorization domain. Then A is a unique factorization domain.
solution_text: Proof: Since A is Noetherian local, the adic completion Â is faithfully flat over A. (1) A is a domain: Â is a domain and A → Â is faithfully flat (hence injective), so A is a domain. (2) A is Noetherian, so every non-zero non-unit element factors into irreducibles (ACC on principal ideals). (3) Every height-1 prime ideal of A is principal: Let p be a height-1 prime of A. By going-down for flat extensions, pÂ has height 1 in Â. Since Â is UFD, every height-1 prime is principal, so pÂ = (π) for some π. Since A is Noetherian, p is finitely generated, and principality descends through faithfully flat extensions for finitely generated ideals, so p is principal. (4) Every irreducible element of A is prime: If a is irreducible, (a) is contained in some height-1 prime p = (π) by Krull's principal ideal theorem, so π | a, and since a is irreducible, (a) = (π) = p is prime. (5) Therefore A is a UFD.
solution_summary: Use faithful flatness of completion to descend the UFD property: A is a domain by faithful flatness, and every height-1 prime of A is principal because height-1 primes descend to height-1 primes in Â (which are principal since Â is UFD) and principality descends through faithful flatness. A Noetherian domain with all height-1 primes principal is a UFD.
